disambiguation.justification: The transaction read surface is heavily redundant: get, filter, search_by_amount, search_by_category, search_by_month, search_by_payee, summary_by_category, summary_by_payee, aggregate, account_flow_summary, and the raw query_run all answer overlapping 'give me transactions/sums' questions with boundaries that are easy to mix up. Name resolution is likewise split between get_id_by_name and entities_search, and account update vs close vs reopen overlap. Descriptions are rich, but the agent must still choose among many near-equivalent paths.

naming_consistency.justification: Most names are actual_<resource>_<verb> snake_case, but the verb position flips (get_context, get_id_by_name, get_balance are action-first while most are resource-first). Snake_case also breaks into camelCase in budgets_holdForNextMonth, getMonth, getMonths, get_all. Readable overall but not a single predictable pattern.

tool_count_appropriateness.justification: At 85 tools the surface is far beyond a well-scoped set for one domain, driven mostly by redundant transaction query variants and per-operation batch siblings. This is an extreme mismatch for the stated purpose and raises selection cost sharply.

completeness.justification: Lifecycle coverage is genuinely broad: full CRUD for accounts, category groups, categories, payees, rules, schedules, tags and transactions, plus transfers, notes, budget months, aggregates and session management. Only minor gaps (no obvious backup/restore beyond budget export/import, no batch delete) keep it from a 5.

summary: This is a feature-complete but sprawling Actual Budget server whose main weakness is a crowded, overlapping transaction-query surface that makes tool selection harder than the individual descriptions suggest. Naming is mostly consistent but slips into camelCase and action-first variants, and 85 tools is excessive for the scope. Completeness is strong, and none of the supplied candidate pairs represent a genuine cheap-path substitution.
